items.description: The ruins of Fort Flacourt are historical remnants of the early French presence in Fort Dauphin.
The Palace of Justice in Amboasary is a notable public building reflecting the regional administrative history.
The Faravohitra Cathedral is a landmark red-brick church in Antananarivo, offering a glimpse into the city's religious history.
Kirindy Forest is a private reserve famous for its population of fossa, the largest predator in Madagascar.
Tsingy de Bemaraha National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage site known for its dramatic 'stone forests'.
The Sahambavy Tea Plantation is the only tea producer in Madagascar, set in a beautiful landscape near Fianarantsoa.
The children's park in Antsirabe is a popular recreational area in the heart of this highlands city.
The orchid park in Andasibe showcases a vast array of Madagascar's unique and beautiful orchid species.
Lemur Island at Vakona Forest Lodge allows visitors to see several species of lemurs in a semi-wild environment.
The city park of Tamatave (Toamasina) provides a green space for relaxation in Madagascar's largest port city.
The coral reefs around Nosy Be are teeming with vibrant marine life, making it a world-class diving spot.
The zoo section of Ranomafana provides an educational look at the unique fauna found within the rainforest.
The rice fields around Antsirabe are a staple of the local landscape and agriculture in the highlands.
Nosy Tanikely is a marine national park renowned for its exceptionally clear waters and rich reef life.
The botanical garden in Toliara features the unique flora of Madagascar's dry south-western region.
